newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling suffers huge loss under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling suffers huge loss under pressure.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling plunged against the dollar on Wednesday because of a shortage of hard currencies after last week's the cancellation of a key aid package by the IMF, commercial dealers said.
The shilling slipped to a commercial average of 67 against the dollar compared to 64.25 at close on Tuesday -- a decline of 4.28 percent, commercial dealers told Reuters.

Commercial dealers said investors were seriously alarmed at President Daniel arap Moi's comments that Kenyans would have to become self-reliant and that the IMF package was insignificant compared to Kenya's total economic requirements.

Moi, appearing to downplay the IMF ruling, told a rally on Tuesday the IMF loan amounted to $205 million when Kenya's was a $3 billion economy. He said Kenya would improve tax collection and commodity exports to meet any shortfalls that may arise from the IMF decision.
On Tuesday, commercial dealers said the shilling was also under pressure because of a shortfall in expected inflows from the coffee and tea sectors -- Kenya's main commodity exports.

"Things are very bad. The market is very nervous," said a dealer, adding that the amount of hard currencies on the market was very little and every dealer sought to cover whatever positions they held.
